newsitem.title: MEXICO: Hurricane Guillermo hovers off Mexico's Pacific coast.
newsitem.headline: Hurricane Guillermo hovers off Mexico's Pacific coast.

text.p: Hurricane Guillermo was upgraded from a tropical storm on Friday after gathering strength off Mexico's Pacific coast, officials said.

Shipping warnings were posted along the entire length of Mexico's western coast, with Guillermo dumping heavy rains and whipping up sea swells of up to 12 feet (four meters), the National Meteorological Service said.
Guillermo was centred 360 miles (580 km) south-southwest of the glitzy tourist resort Acapulco, moving westerly almost parallel to the coast at 13 mph (20 kph), it added.
Officials expected the storm to pick up more steam later on Friday and pack sustained winds of 81 mph (130 kph) with gusts of 100 mph (160 kph) by 7 p.m. local time (0001 GMT on Saturday).

No word was given of when or where the storm might hit land, but heavy rains and flash flooding were reported in the southwestern states of Guerrero and Michoacan and the western state of Jalisco, the service said.
"It is recommended that shipping in the Mexican Pacific take extreme caution because of the rains, winds and strong sea swells," the service said.
Guerrero, Michoacan and Jalisco are predominantly agriculture states, growing grains, coffee, sugar and raising livestock.

No oil or gas is produced in the region, and Hurricane Guillermo is far from the only Pacific oil port of Salina Cruz. All ports remained open to shipping, the Communications and Transport Ministry said in a statement.
